vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mailbox-bot
Version: 2.0.1

The skill bundle is classified as benign. All code and instructions, including the agent-facing instructions in SKILL.md, are directly aligned with the stated purpose of providing a physical logistics endpoint for AI agents. The skill makes legitimate API calls to `https://mailbox.bot` for waitlist signup, package listing, and forwarding, using a specific environment variable (`MAILBOX_BOT_API_KEY`) for authentication. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, persistence mechanisms, or deceptive prompt injection attempts against the agent. The `curl` commands are well-defined and target a consistent domain, and the instructions for the agent are clear and non-malicious.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions, requirements, and behavior are internally consistent with a service that offers a physical fulfillment endpoint for agents; it is an instruction-only skill that does not request unexpected system access or credentials.

dimensions.detail: The name/description promise (provide a shipping address, scan/photograph packages, webhook notifications, forward/store/return) matches the SKILL.md and README. There are no unrelated env vars, binaries, or install steps requested that would contradict the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs agents to perform onboarding (KYC via Stripe Identity), to use an API key when available, and to expect webhooks with photos and metadata. These actions (KYC, photographing/opening package contents, sending webhooks) are within the described service but involve sensitive PII and package contents—users should be aware that onboarding shares identity/payment data and that package contents may be opened/photographed and transmitted in webhook payloads.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec, no code files), so nothing is written to disk or automatically installed. The README suggests using an external 'clawhub' CLI for publishing, but that is for publishing/installation by maintainers and is not part of runtime behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required env vars or credentials are declared. The SKILL.md references an optional MAILBOX_BOT_API_KEY for live API access only, which is proportional to the described API usage. Onboarding and KYC will require external identity/payment credentials, which are required by the external service (not the skill itself).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and is user-invocable; it does not request persistent system privileges, nor does it modify other skills or system config. Autonomous invocation by the model is enabled by default (normal) but not combined with elevated privileges here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: provide a physical fulfillment endpoint, scan/photograph packages, and post webhook notifications. Before installing or using it, consider: (1) Onboarding requires KYC (Stripe Identity) and payment information—be prepared to share identity documents with the external service. (2) Packages may be opened/photographed and those photos/metadata will be sent in webhooks—ensure your webhook endpoints and data handling meet your privacy/security needs. (3) Confirm the service terms (what they will store, retention period, liability as bailee) and whether shipping certain items is allowed. (4) Verify the API domain and endpoints (https://mailbox.bot) and the process for obtaining/revoking API keys. (5) If you plan to allow autonomous agents to request forwarding/receiving, restrict what agents are allowed to order/receive to avoid unintended purchases or receipt of regulated items.
